must_remember: Beat frequency is given by the absolute difference between two interfering frequencies: $f_{beat} = |f_1 - f_2|$.
The persistence of human hearing is approximately $0.1\text{ s}$, meaning beats above $10\text{ Hz}$ are not distinguishable as separate pulses.
Loading a tuning fork with wax increases its effective mass and decreases its natural frequency ($f' < f$).
Filing a tuning fork reduces its mass and stiffness, which increases its natural frequency ($f'' > f$).
Beats are produced by the superposition of two waves traveling in the same direction with nearly equal frequencies.

glossary.meaning: The number of intensity maxima heard per second, equal to $|f_1 - f_2|$.
The retention of a sensory impression in the human ear for about $1/10\text{th}$ of a second.
Adding mass (such as wax) to the prongs of a tuning fork to lower its frequency.
Scraping or removing metal from the prongs of a tuning fork to raise its frequency.
